examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Degree counts schema attributes; cardinality counts tuples. Keys are minimal uniqueness constraints, while superkeys may contain extra attributes. Primary-key attributes cannot be NULL. SQL tables can use bag semantics even though mathematical relations are sets; SELECT without DISTINCT does not implicitly remove duplicates.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A relation has 5 attributes and two candidate keys AB and AC. How many superkeys contain at least one of them?

**Answer: 12.** Supersets of AB number 2^(5−2)=8; supersets of AC also 8. Supersets of ABC were counted twice and number 2^(5−3)=4. Inclusion–exclusion gives 8+8−4=12.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
This count assumes these are the only candidate keys. Any additional minimal key can add superkeys not covered by those two families.

Minimal means no attribute can be removed while retaining uniqueness; it does not mean shortest among all keys.
